label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / Al Jazeera — 12–13 August 2026
contestNote: DRC: 4,665 confirmed across 54 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and — as of 13 August — Bas-Uélé) as of 12 August, published 13 August. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths). France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported given ongoing active transmission and community mistrust limiting detection.
delta: +4,284 DRC since 5 June (381 → 4,665); Uganda outbreak closed 28 July
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly twelvefold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5) → 4,566 (August 12) → 4,665 (August 13). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). Africa CDC warns it could become the largest ever recorded if not slowed.

label: Lab-Confirmed Cases (2026 Outbreak — DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC — 12–13 August 2026
deltaNote: The 12 August DRC situation report recorded an increase of 99 confirmed cases and 56 deaths from the prior day alone. 570 patients currently hospitalized in isolation in DRC. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya warned on 13 August: 'If we do not stop this outbreak, it will last more than a year and will be the largest in the world.'

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC — 12–13 August 2026
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 2,184 DRC + 2 Uganda = 2,186 total as of 12 August. CFR (confirmed): ~46.8% (2,184/4,665 DRC). Deaths rose from 1,000 to 2,000 in under a month — versus over 12 months for the 2018–2020 Kivu outbreak and nearly 5 months for the 2014 West Africa epidemic — the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's recorded history. WHO reports 60–70% of deaths occur in communities away from treatment centers.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5) → 2,128 (August 12) → 2,184 (August 13). 151+ confirmed cases among healthcare workers, 44 deaths (29% CFR among HCWs).

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC — 12–13 August 2026
contestNote: Crude CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's 5 August report put CFR at 45.6% (1,850/4,053). CFR has climbed steadily as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones, now reaching a sixth province (Bas-Uélé). BDBV historically 25–47% CFR, but this outbreak's crude CFR now exceeds the historical range, likely reflecting under-ascertainment of milder cases as much as true severity.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — WHO/DRC Advance Phase 3 Ervebo Trial Talks
value: WHO and DRC advancing talks to launch Phase 3 Ervebo ring trial (12 Aug 2026)
source: STAT News / WHO Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccine Prioritization / Gavi — 7–12 August 2026
contestNote: 7 August: WHO's TAG-CVP recommended prioritizing Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV, licensed for Zaire ebolavirus, ~84% effective against that species) for a Phase 3 ring-vaccination trial in DRC to test cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus. 12 August: STAT News reported WHO and DRC authorities are advancing talks to launch the trial, randomizing individual contacts of cases to vaccine or placebo, with Gavi's ~500,000-dose Ervebo stockpile available. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. WHO cautions efficacy against transmission/infection may be low even if protection against death is achieved. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV and IAVI's rVSV BDBV remain in earlier-stage human trials and may be added to the trial later.
delta: Reversal of 28 May off-label-use ban — Ervebo trial talks now actively advancing
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation and 12 August trial talks are steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 6 DRC provinces (54 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / Africa CDC — 12–13 August 2026
delta: Expanded to a sixth province (Bas-Uélé) on 13 August 2026
deltaNote: Ituri Province: ~87-88% of all confirmed cases and deaths. North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo added by 11 July. On 13 August a death in Buta, capital of Bas-Uélé province, marked the outbreak's spread to a sixth province — the victim had traveled from Isiro in Haut-Uélé. 54 of 151 health zones now affected. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over 28 July. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: ~82.7% of identified contacts under active follow-up
delta: Coverage improved from ~45% (June) but 60-70% of new cases are still occurring outside monitored contacts
deltaNote: ECDC reported active follow-up at 82.7% of identified contacts as of 10 August, up from 75.5% (Ituri), 74.6% (North Kivu), 80.6% (Haut-Uélé) and 66.2% (Tshopo) province-level rates in late July — still below the 90%+ threshold needed for rapid suppression. Mercy Corps separately warned 60-70% of new cases are recorded outside monitored contacts, with confirmed cases now just 35km from the South Sudan border. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following the 28 July outbreak-end declaration. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
